Its composer, as creating says, is drawn where it was clicked, at the foot in the line's place, or at the top, above the first card, from "+ Add": a story card, as the parts draw one, its title a text box in the card's title text, with the focus ring around the card, and beneath it, muted, "Enter to add, Escape to cancel"; the cards below it move down to make room, and the list scrolls to keep it in view. 86:Each column scrolls up and down on its own, its heading staying at its top while its cards scroll beneath it, inside the list's rounded corners, with the [Scrollbar](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) shown along the list's right, inside it, while it holds more than fits. The board scrolls sideways when its columns are wider than the tab, with the [Scrollbar](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) along its foot; while they fit, it doesn't scroll. The wheel and the trackpad scroll what is under the pointer, each part of the board on its own. A vertical wheel turn or two-finger swipe over a column, its heading included, scrolls only that column up or down; it never scrolls the board sideways, and it never passes on to the board, not when the column is at its top or its end, nor when it has nothing to scroll. The horizontal wheel never scrolls a column up or down, and it moves the board the way it is turned, right moving the board right and left moving it left. A vertical wheel turn over the board outside every column, on its padding, in the 16 pixel gaps between columns, or in the space beside the last column, scrolls the board sideways instead, as Trello does, down moving it right and up left. A diagonal trackpad swipe over a column scrolls the column up or down and the board sideways together, each by its own share of the swipe, the up and down share to the column and the sideways share to the board. Scrolling over the side panel, the pause bar, or the bulk bar never moves the board or any of its columns: the side panel scrolls only itself, and the two bars scroll nothing. Every card's state reads the same way, as below, and every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.
87:The board is kept as it was left while Planning's tab stays open, as the [Body](../application/Body.md#body) keeps a tab. Selecting another tab and then Planning's again shows the board scrolled sideways exactly where it was left, and every column scrolled up or down exactly where it was, at once, with nothing animating, sliding, or scrolling into view, as though the tab had never been left; nothing is scrolled to its start or to a card on the way back. The side panel opening or closing in the meantime, as a story opened from outside the board, changes only the board's sideways scroll, as far as the panel's opening or closing needs, as motion says, and shows it already settled when the tab is back; every column keeps its own scroll through it. The scroll is the board's own, kept only while its tab is open, and never saved with the plan, in `order.json` or anywhere else: closing Planning's tab and opening it again, or reloading the window, starts the board at its left edge and every column at its top.
88:The side panel is the one place anything opens: an open story, Draft stories, and Research, never beneath a heading or a card, and never in a popup or over the board. A composer is not an opened story but a card being written, and is the one thing drawn in a list, where its story will sit. It is docked at the right of Planning's tab, 400 pixels wide, as tall as the tab, from the tab bar down to the chat input, a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its left edge, and it scrolls up and down on its own, its heading staying at its top, with the [Scrollbar](../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar) along its right while it holds more than fits. Only one thing is in it at a time: opening a story, drafting, or research replaces whatever it held, and closing it leaves nothing there. While it is open the board narrows to the space left of it, its columns keeping their width and scrolling sideways as ever when they no longer fit; the panel never covers the board, and the board never covers it. Closed, it takes no space and the board fills the tab again. It slides in and out at the right, as motion says.
89:While paused, the pause bar runs across the top of the whole board, above every column, as the paused section says, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it. Each column is headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use the same five parts, below.
94:- A list: one per column, as the layout places it, 320 pixels wide and as tall as the board, on the theme's recessed surface, one step from the base, with no border, the theme's pressed bevel inside its edges, its corners rounded 8 pixels, 8 pixels of padding; a 2 pixel edge along its top, in its status icon's colour laid over the recessed surface at 50%, as the layout says, the column's one look of its own; its heading row at its top, as the layout says, then its cards, or its empty state centred beneath its heading; its heading's status icon one per column, each always the same: the Backlog a dashed circle in the theme's tertiary text colour; Next sprint an empty circle in the theme's secondary text colour; Current sprint a half-filled circle in the theme's accent; Done a filled circle with a check in the theme's success colour; and Findings a magnifying glass in the theme's secondary text colour; each, with the list's top edge in its colour, telling its column apart at a glance while still only repeating the column's name, never standing for it alone

101:While any card is selected, the bulk bar runs across the board's foot, beneath its columns, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it nor over the board: a row 40 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its top, the columns shortening to make room as it slides up in motion's quick motion, and lengthening again as it slides away once nothing is selected. Moved stories stay selected, duplicates are not selected, and the originals stay so. The bar has no Send and sends nothing: a story still reaches work only through the sprint, as the sprint says.
102:Dragging a selected card by its grip carries the whole selection, in its order: the other selected cards leave their places as it lifts, their columns closing up, and the lifted copy is the grabbed card, as motion draws it, with the cards it carries stacked a few pixels behind it and their count beside its title. Dragging a card that isn't selected moves it alone and leaves the selection as it is.
108:- Empty: a single muted line, centred in the column beneath its heading, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration

Send sprint to start one." in Current sprint, and "Nothing done yet." in Done; loading, while the plan is read on opening, a few skeleton cards in each column, never an empty column; error, when the plan can't be read or saved, saying which file and why, with "Try again"

content.text:
Each kanban column now has its own look, as the updated spec describes:

- **Sunk into the board:** each list keeps its recessed surface and still has no border, but now draws the theme's pressed bevel inside its 8 pixel corners.
- **Coloured top edge:** each list has a 2 pixel edge along its top, above the heading and inside its rounded corners. Its colour is the status icon's colour at 50% over the recessed surface: tertiary text for Backlog, secondary text for Next sprint and Findings, the accent for Current sprint, and success for Done.
- **Icons:** `column_icon` now gets its colour from the same per-column function as the edge, so the two always match.

The width, gaps and corners are unchanged. Cards, headings, the empty state and the drag placeholder's well surface are untouched. To draw a bevel that follows rounded corners, I added a small `rounded_bevel` helper to `src/theme.rs`.

**Tests:** I added three, covering dark and light mode. They check each column's colour and edge at half strength, and that neighbouring columns differ. They check the edge is fainter and thinner than a card's hover, selected surface, focus ring and the open story's 3 pixel accent line. They also check that lists use the pressed bevel. They pass, along with the theme tests.

**The tests couldn't run as-is here:** this session isn't allowed to read `.suspense/system-prompts`, and the build embeds those files. So I ran the tests in a temporary worktree with empty stand-ins for them, then removed it.

**Six other planning tests fail:** for example `a_dragged_card_finds_its_gap_in_the_column_under_it`, and two that panic with "test_support requires an existing ElementId". I took out the new list drawing and five of them failed the same way. The sixth (`proposals_reach_the_plan_only_once_accepted`) passed on that run, so I can't say for sure it isn't related.

The code follows the spec, and the spec didn't disagree with the prompt.
